newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE warns of deepening crisis in Albania.
newsitem.headline: OSCE warns of deepening crisis in Albania.

text.p: Europe's security forum said on Wednesday it was deeply worried about the increasing violence in Albania and warned that the potential for a serious crisis was at hand.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe's current chairman-in-office, Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen, called on all sides in the Balkan state to refrain from violent acts and respect the rule of law.

"The chairman-in-office of the OSCE wishes to express his deep concern about developments in Albania. The potential for a serious crisis is at hand," Petersen said in a statement issued from the organisation's headquarters in Vienna.
"The chairman-in-office calls upon all sides involved to refrain from the use of violence and to respect the rule of law," he added.

Petersen, who took over the chairmanship in January, said the current crisis in Albania, sparked by the collapse of shady pyramid investment schemes, could only be resolved through peaceful dialogue. Albania has been hit by a wave of protests over the past two months by small investors who have been left destitute.

The OSCE produced a scathing report on the conduct of Albania's general election last May, pointing out serious irregularities and intimidation during polling. President Sali Berisha's right-wing Democratic Party won most seats in the 140-member parliament.
